members.name: onCleanup
members.description: Registers a cleanup callback that runs automatically when the plugin is disabled, even if `activate` later throws. Callbacks run in reverse registration order. Use this for helpers created during activation instead of returning one large cleanup closure. The cleanup returned by `activate` is also supported.

members.name: file
members.type:
{ createBlobUrl(dataUri: string): Promise<string>; revokeObjectURL(url: string): void;
  }
members.description: File utilities for working with file-type settings. When a plugin declares a **file** setting, the user picks a file and the plugin receives a base64 data URI (e.g. "data:image/png;base64,...") as the setting value. Use `createBlobUrl()` to convert it to a blob URL for use in CSS or image elements. The file is read at pick time, not at runtime — there is no generic file-reading command. Plugins execute as trusted page code. Data URIs may be at most 8 MiB; other setting values are limited to 64 KiB.

HTTPInspector.name: HTTPInspector
HTTPInspector.description: Inspects HTTP requests flowing through the application via `fetch()`. Provides access to observed incoming (response) and outgoing (request) messages. Requests and responses can be modified using interceptors.

members.name: exchanges
members.description: Complete HTTP exchanges (request + response). This channel fires after the response is received.

members.name: outgoing
members.type:
{ subscribe(handler: HTTPOutgoingMessageHandler): () => void; use(interceptor: HTTPOutgoingInterceptor): () => void;
  }
members.description: Outgoing HTTP requests (fires immediately when the request is sent).

members.name: responses
members.description: HTTP responses that can be intercepted and modified before delivery. Interceptors run asynchronously after the response is received but before it is returned to the caller.

HTTPMessage.name: HTTPMessage
HTTPMessage.description: A single observed HTTP exchange with request and response metadata. The `requestBody` and `responseBody` fields are immutable snapshots captured at the time of observation. For binary payloads (ArrayBuffer, ArrayBufferView), the data is copied so that mutating the original argument does not corrupt the observed snapshot. For Blob payloads, the data is represented as a `BlobSnapshot` since Blobs cannot be read synchronously. Consumers should treat body fields as read-only.
HTTPMessage.declaration:
export type HTTPMessage = { url: string; method: string; requestHeaders: [string, string][]; requestBody?: string | ArrayBuffer | BlobSnapshot; status: number; statusText: string; responseHeaders: [string, string][]; responseBody?: string | ArrayBuffer | BlobSnapshot; timestamp: number; duration: number;
};

members.name: url
members.description: The request URL.

members.name: method
members.description: HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.).

members.name: requestHeaders
members.description: Request headers as an ordered array of [name, value] pairs.

members.name: requestBody
members.description: Request body, captured as an immutable snapshot (undefined for no-body methods).

members.name: status
members.description: Response status code (e.g. 200, 404).

members.name: statusText
members.description: Response status text (e.g. "OK", "Not Found").

members.name: responseHeaders
members.description: Response headers as an ordered array of [name, value] pairs.

members.name: responseBody
members.description: Response body, captured as an immutable snapshot.

members.name: timestamp
members.description: When the request was sent (epoch ms).

members.name: duration
members.description: Duration of the request in milliseconds.

HTTPOutgoingMessage.name: HTTPOutgoingMessage
HTTPOutgoingMessage.description: A single observed outgoing HTTP request (before response is available). Used by the outgoing channel so that subscribers fire immediately when the request is sent, without waiting for the response.
HTTPOutgoingMessage.declaration:
export type HTTPOutgoingMessage = { url: string; method: string; requestHeaders: [string, string][]; requestBody?: string | ArrayBuffer | BlobSnapshot; timestamp: number;
};

members.name: url
members.description: The request URL.

members.name: method
members.description: HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.).

members.name: requestHeaders
members.description: Request headers as an ordered array of [name, value] pairs.

members.name: requestBody
members.description: Request body, captured as an immutable snapshot (undefined for no-body methods).

members.name: timestamp
members.description: When the request was sent (epoch ms).

HTTPOutgoingRequestPatch.name: HTTPOutgoingRequestPatch
HTTPOutgoingRequestPatch.description: A set of overrides returned by an outgoing HTTP interceptor. Omitted fields keep the current request value. `headers` replaces the full header set; use the interceptor's `requestHeaders` to build a modified set. `body` replaces the request body; pass `null` to remove it.
HTTPOutgoingRequestPatch.declaration:
export type HTTPOutgoingRequestPatch = { url?: string | URL; method?: string; headers?: HeadersInit; body?: BodyInit | null;
};

members.name: url
members.description: Replacement URL. A `URL` is converted to a string.

members.name: method
members.description: Replacement HTTP method.

members.name: headers
members.description: Replacement headers.

members.name: body
members.description: Replacement body. Pass `null` to send no body.

HTTPOutgoingInterceptor.name: HTTPOutgoingInterceptor
HTTPOutgoingInterceptor.description: Interceptor for outgoing HTTP requests. Receives the request metadata and may return overrides to change the URL, method, headers, or body before the request is transmitted. Interceptors run asynchronously in registration order. Each interceptor receives the request as modified by the previous one. - Returning `undefined` (void) means no change. - Returning a patch applies those fields to the current request. - If an interceptor throws or returns an invalid patch, every modification in the chain is discarded and the original request is sent unchanged. Request delivery is never suppressed by an interceptor.

HTTPResponseInterceptor.name: HTTPResponseInterceptor
HTTPResponseInterceptor.description: Interceptor for HTTP responses. Receives the complete exchange (request + response) and may return a modified `Response` object to replace the original response. Interceptors run asynchronously in registration order after the response is received but before it is delivered to the caller. - Returning `undefined` (void) means no change — the original response is kept. - Returning a `Response` object replaces the original response. - If an interceptor throws, the original response is delivered and the error is logged. Response delivery is never suppressed by an interceptor.

HTTPMessageHandler.name: HTTPMessageHandler
HTTPMessageHandler.description: Callback invoked when a new HTTP exchange is observed.

HTTPOutgoingMessageHandler.name: HTTPOutgoingMessageHandler
HTTPOutgoingMessageHandler.description: Callback invoked when a new outgoing HTTP request is observed.

WebSocketInspector.name: WebSocketInspector
WebSocketInspector.description: Inspects WebSocket messages flowing through the application. Provides access to observed incoming and outgoing messages. Messages can be modified before delivery or transmission using interceptors.

members.name: incoming
members.type:
{ subscribe(handler: WebSocketMessageHandler): () => void; use(interceptor: WebSocketIncomingInterceptor): () => void;
  }
members.description: Messages received by the application from a WebSocket server.

members.name: outgoing
members.type:
{ subscribe(handler: WebSocketMessageHandler): () => void; use(interceptor: WebSocketOutgoingInterceptor): () => void;
  }
members.description: Messages sent by the application through a WebSocket connection.

WebSocketMessage.name: WebSocketMessage
WebSocketMessage.description: A single observed WebSocket message with basic connection metadata. The `data` field is an immutable snapshot of the message payload at the time it was observed. For binary payloads (ArrayBuffer, ArrayBufferView), the data is copied so that mutating the original send argument does not corrupt the observed snapshot. For Blob payloads, the data is represented as a `BlobSnapshot` since Blobs cannot be read synchronously. Consumers should treat `data` as read-only.
WebSocketMessage.declaration:
export type WebSocketMessage = { url: string; data: string | ArrayBuffer | BlobSnapshot; timestamp: number;
};

members.name: url
members.description: The URL the WebSocket was created with.

members.name: data
members.description: The message payload, captured as an immutable snapshot. - Strings remain strings. - ArrayBuffer and ArrayBufferView payloads are copied into a new ArrayBuffer. - Blob payloads are represented as a BlobSnapshot (cannot be read synchronously).

members.name: timestamp
members.description: When the message was observed (epoch ms).

WebSocketMessageHandler.name: WebSocketMessageHandler
WebSocketMessageHandler.description: Callback invoked when a new WebSocket message is observed.

BlobSnapshot.name: BlobSnapshot
BlobSnapshot.description: Represents a Blob payload that could not be read synchronously. Since reading a Blob requires an asynchronous API, the inspector stores a snapshot describing the blob's metadata instead of its contents.
BlobSnapshot.declaration:
export type BlobSnapshot = { __blob: true; type: string; size: number;
};

members.name: __blob
members.description: Identifies this as a Blob snapshot.

members.name: type
members.description: The Blob's reported type (MIME type), if available.

members.name: size
members.description: The Blob's reported size in bytes.

WebSocketOutgoingInterceptor.name: WebSocketOutgoingInterceptor
WebSocketOutgoingInterceptor.description: Interceptor for outgoing WebSocket messages. Receives the message data and connection metadata, and may return a replacement payload to send instead. Interceptors run synchronously in registration order before the original `send()` call. Each interceptor receives the latest payload produced by the previous interceptor. - Returning `undefined` (void) means no change — the current payload is kept. - Returning a valid WebSocket payload (`string`, `ArrayBuffer`, `ArrayBufferView`, or `Blob`) replaces the current payload. - If an interceptor throws, all modifications from the entire interception chain are discarded and the original payload is sent unchanged. - If an interceptor returns an invalid type, it is treated as a failure: the entire chain is discarded and the original payload is sent. Message delivery is never suppressed by an interceptor.

WebSocketIncomingInterceptor.name: WebSocketIncomingInterceptor
WebSocketIncomingInterceptor.description: Interceptor for incoming WebSocket messages. Receives the message and may return replacement data to deliver to the application instead. Interceptors run synchronously in registration order as each message is received. Each interceptor receives the latest payload produced by the previous interceptor. - Returning `undefined` (void) means no change — the current payload is kept. - Returning a valid WebSocket payload (`string`, `ArrayBuffer`, `ArrayBufferView`, or `Blob`) replaces the delivered payload. - If an interceptor throws or returns an invalid type, all modifications from the chain are discarded and the original payload is delivered. Message delivery is never suppressed by an interceptor. Because message delivery is synchronous, returning a promise is not supported.
